evidence.title: Hamblen County adopts request for one-year moratorium on high-intensity electrical-load facilities
evidence.supports: Describes the proposed moratorium's scope as 'high-intensity electrical-load facilities' with data centers cited as the driving example; does not describe battery storage as an independently regulated land use, consistent with the row's own legal_basis phrase 'ancillary battery systems' referring to a facility's own on-site backup power equipment.
evidence.quote: The Public Services Committee voted to request an interim one-year moratorium on high-intensity electrical-load facilities — the ordinance language cited data centers as an example — while county staff and the planning commission draft permanent zoning regulations.

decisions.notes: SECTOR_CHECK not changed: the row's own legal_basis text describes the draft ordinance's definition as covering 'data centers, crypto mining, HPC, ancillary battery systems' -- the word 'ancillary' indicates battery systems that are accessory/backup equipment attached to a high-intensity electrical load facility (e.g. on-site UPS/backup batteries), not a standalone battery-storage (BESS) development, which is what the battery_storage sector tag denotes elsewhere in this inventory. Could not retrieve the draft ordinance's own text to confirm this reading directly: hamblencountytn.gov returned a 502 Bad Gateway / repeated timeouts on every attempt (direct fetch, browser mode, and a Wayback Machine lookup only returned a March 2026 snapshot predating the ordinance), and a Facebook post reportedly quoting the draft ordinance was behind a login wall. Left sectors unchanged on the strength of the 'ancillary' language and the CitizenPortal.ai committee recap, which frames the whole ordinance around 'high-intensity electrical-load facilities' generally rather than battery storage as its own use. Separately (not the assigned flag but relevant to the row's own [VERIFY] marker): found a Kingsport-area Citizen Tribune headline indicating the County Commission 'passed a moratorium on high intensity electrical-load facilities' the night of Thursday, Aug. 20, 2026 (article published Aug. 22, 2026), which would mean the moratorium has since moved from Planning-Commission-recommended to Commission-adopted; the full article text was inaccessible (accessibility-widget page shell only, paywalled). A separate item also references a Sept. 24, 2026 hearing on the same 'pause for big power-use facilities,' which is inconsistent with a completed Aug. 20 adoption unless that Sept. 24 date concerns a different, later step (e.g. the permanent zoning ordinance). Did not change enacted_status/date_enacted_iso given this conflict and inability to read either source in full; flagging for the coordinator/a future pass.

evidence.title: Commissioners Say No to Data Centers

decisions.notes: SECTOR_CHECK resolved: every source describing the resolution's own operative scope (Upper Cumberland's News Leader, Hoodline, Sparta Live) characterizes it as a ban on 'data centers'/'AI and data center facilities,' never as separately naming or defining cryptocurrency mining. The 'crypto' mention in the row's own current_status is about the specific Pleasant Hill Road project that later surfaced as a rumored 4.9 MW facility and became a test of the ban's enforceability -- a triggering/background project mention, not the resolution's stated coverage (and per Hoodline, the whole point of the controversy is that this project may evade the ban entirely on a parcel-size technicality, regardless of sector). The original resolution text itself could not be located (as the row's own legal_basis already notes), so this rests on consistent secondary reporting rather than a primary source; confidence set accordingly. sectors stays ["data_center"].
